title: New license plate scanning parking garage system raises City Councilor concerns - Cville Right Now
summary: Charlottesville City Council spent nearly an hour at its first 2026 meeting discussing concerns about a new license-plate-scanning parking garage payment system operated by Metropolis, which acquired the city's previous parking vendor SP-Plus. Councilors raised concerns about data retention, access, and surveillance, drawing parallels to prior community concerns about ALPRs like Flock and Peregrine, while staff defended the system as a needed modernization.

key_quotes.quote: I think after the community had such concerns about automatic license plates readers, Flock, Peregrine, to implement this on the part of city government is hypocrisy and I think hard to defend.
The business model is very new and explicit of establishing a nationwide monopoly in parking management, using AI to mass surveil customers and then monetizing it.
But I am paranoid about where the data is stored and who has access to the data as it's stored.
providing alternatives that reduce the risks associated with ALPR technology and data capture
